title: Choose the living Product Passport composition
question: The forest, landing-page typography, purple glass, and requested component stack are now fixed. Choose the composition to carry into the production Product Passport, or steer a combination.

options.label: Violet Grotto
options.lineage: A specimen chamber cut into a bioluminescent forest
options.thesis: The product owns a complete living left bay while the trusted measurement sits in one calm glass instrument on the right.
options.viewport: A strict forest/specimen split: full can stage left, landing-page headline and 240 mg instrument right, evidence grid below.
options.risk: The two-bay split is the most legible option, but also the most composed and least immersive.

options.label: Night Conservatory
options.lineage: A glasshouse section drawn through a living nocturnal canopy
options.thesis: One uninterrupted forest room holds title, specimen, and measurement as three depths of the same scene.
options.viewport: The title lives in the canopy, the can crosses the structural glass rails, and the caffeine readout floats as one deep instrument.
options.risk: This is the most cinematic option; title and specimen overlap deliberately and need disciplined responsive choreography.

options.label: Herbarium Ledger
options.lineage: A botanical evidence sheet paired with a living specimen window
options.thesis: The institutional record becomes an editorial ledger while the forest remains a vivid, full-height specimen field.
options.viewport: A precise record column leads on the left; the complete product rises in a saturated forest aperture on the right.
options.risk: The editorial hierarchy feels most institutional, but it gives less opening emphasis to the caffeine instrument than Violet Grotto.
